subject.title: feat(chat): rewind and fork a session from a message bubble

question: Should OpenClaw expose these additive core gateway operations and persistent-session mutations as the supported per-message rewind/fork product contract after the locked-session boundary is repaired?
rationale: This is a new user-facing core capability with two public RPCs and durable session-state semantics; code review can identify the lock bypass but cannot decide whether the expanded long-term protocol and lifecycle contract is desired.

options.title: Sponsor the core feature after repair
options.body: Retain the proposed core direction, reject locked entries before mutation, add regression coverage, and require live Control UI proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep only a safer UI/session operation with reduced public protocol exposure if maintainers do not want two new long-lived gateway methods.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause this PR if the per-message transcript-branch workflow is not currently a supported core product priority.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core feature after repair
recommendation.body: Retain the proposed core direction, reject locked entries before mutation, add regression coverage, and require live Control UI proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor most directly to the proposed session and chat implementation, while broader ownership could not be established in this review environment.
